requirements.requirement: node1 and node2 share a single address on the private network that only one of them answers at a time
requirements.summary: keepalived VRRP configured via UCI on both OpenWrt nodes with virtual_router_id 51, shared VIP 10.100.232.250/24 on br-lan (cmd-a867bd2f75ee4cfe, cmd-9fe7010c2fce44e2). After starting keepalived, node1 (priority 150, MASTER) holds the VIP while node2 (priority 100, BACKUP) shows only its own address with no VIP (cmd-1fc6ebfa5511487f vs cmd-ed66ccdf88664bab), confirming mutual exclusivity.

requirements.requirement: The other node takes over the shared address automatically when the first stops serving
requirements.summary: Stopping keepalived on node1 (MASTER, cmd-7b3b928b39034a04) is followed within 5s by node2 acquiring the VIP with no manual intervention (cmd-9bb89478a1dc46c3). Restarting node1's keepalived (cmd-d6e04ccd5176467d) shows it preempt back to MASTER and reclaim the VIP while node2 cleanly relinquishes it (cmd-d2dd7d8e386e47ea, cmd-59982e152ac64fd9), demonstrating automatic bidirectional handover.

requirements.requirement: node3 keeps reaching the shared address across one such transition
requirements.summary: A continuous timestamped ping from node3 to the VIP (cmd-8f9b373e10d74523) was left running across the node1 stop/node2 promotion and the node1 restart/preemption back. The captured log (cmd-292d7b15ada641e0, cmd-025be5fc29614f53, cmd-b838a822b9e44907) shows an unbroken sequence icmp_seq 1-42 with 0% loss spanning both transition boundaries (node1 stop at 13:08:53, node2 promoted by 13:08:56-13:09:01 window, node1 restarted 13:09:15), directly demonstrating uninterrupted reachability through the failover and failback.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task were directly demonstrated with real, bounded transitions rather than just configuration: a single shared VIP on node1/node2 answered exclusively by the active peer, automatic VRRP-based failover in both directions (stop/promote and restart/preempt), and an unbroken node3 ping log (icmp_seq 1-42, 0% loss) spanning the entire failover-and-failback window. The independent node-restart evidence protocol was also completed for all three nodes with matching pre/post boot identities, reboot acknowledgements, and confirmed post-reboot recovery of keepalived state and VIP reachability, consistent with the fixed after-executor snapshot's boot-identity values.
limitations: Node2's post-restart listening-sockets check returned an empty/failed result (rc=255) in the final lifecycle snapshot; this appears to be a transient command failure rather than an actual service problem, since keepalived status and VIP absence on node2 were independently confirmed as expected (BACKUP state), but it could not be cross-verified via the socket listing.

The task instruction did not require surviving a full node reboot for the VIP/failover behavior itself; the node-restart protocol evidence is assessed only as supplemental, provider-wide evidence quality, not as part of the material task outcomes.

operational_hygiene.summary: Executor actions were tightly scoped to the task: package install, UCI config writes, and keepalived start/stop/restart cycles used to both configure and demonstrate failover, all with a clear causal link to a material outcome. One reboot attempt on node1 using nohup failed silently because nohup was unavailable (cmd-5e0c5df690d94550, confirmed via /tmp/reboot.log content in cmd-424a109926ab4eac showing 'nohup: not found'); this left no state change (boot_id unchanged across three follow-up checks) and was immediately corrected with a working 'sh -c sleep 1; reboot' invocation (cmd-e7a3f79de9694e89), so it is a non-mutating failed attempt rather than residue. The lifecycle diff shows only expected keepalived-related additions in /tmp and package-health listings on node1/node2 (config files, pid/lock files, apk manifest entries) with no unrelated or abandoned files. dnsmasq on node1 began listening on the new VIP address (10.100.232.250:53) as an automatic consequence of the VIP being assigned to br-lan, not a separate action by the executor, and is confined to the already-isolated private network. No destructive, broad, or security-weakening mutations were observed, and the vip_ping.log/pid artifacts on node3 were cleaned up (killed) before node3's own reboot cleared /tmp.
